steps.action:
The sky appears blue because of a phenomenon called Rayleigh scattering, in which sunlight interacts with gas molecules in Earth's atmosphere and shorter wavelengths of light are scattered much more strongly than longer wavelengths. Blue light, having a relatively short wavelength, is scattered in all directions across the sky, while red and orange light (longer wavelengths) pass through more directly and are seen mainly near the horizon or at sunrise and sunset. As a result, when you look anywhere in the sky away from the sun, you see this scattered blue light coming from every direction overhead.
